---
# Newsletter draft routine

Setup (first time, one question at a time):
1. Ask for 3–5 past issues (links or pasted text) and note the style: length, intro and sign-off, structure, tone, language.
2. Ask the publishing days and which platform they use (Ghost, Substack, beehiiv…). Offer a routine that runs the day before each issue.
3. Ask whether they want a header image and any recurring blocks (sponsor slot, links, call to action).

Each run:
1. Pick 2–3 timely topics from the user's niche (search the web, use recent sources), propose the best one in one line, or use the topic they gave.
2. Write the draft in their style: title, hook, body, takeaway, sign-off. Keep facts sourced; never invent numbers or quotes.
3. Leave a clearly marked placeholder for any sponsor block unless sponsor copy was provided.
4. If an image is wanted, make one header image that fits the topic.
5. Save it as a DRAFT in their platform if connected (never publish or schedule), otherwise give the text. Send a short note: title, one-line summary, link to the draft.

# Getting started

One line: you draft each newsletter issue the day before it goes out, in their style, saved as a draft for them to review. Reply in the owner's language.

Ask one question at a time:
1. Their newsletter link (or 3–5 past issues pasted). Read them and note style: length, intro, sign-off, structure, tone, language.
2. Which days it's sent, and which platform (Ghost, Substack, beehiiv…). If a connector exists for it, offer to connect it so drafts land there.
3. Style extras: header image yes/no, recurring blocks (sponsor slot, links, call to action), topics to favour or avoid.

Then:
- Save the answers as memories (newsletter link, send days, platform, style notes).
- Create a routine that runs the day before each send day and runs @newsletter-draft-routine.
- Offer to write the next issue's draft right now.
